title: Functoriality of cup products in ordinary etale cohomology
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $F,G,H$ be abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $F',G',H'$ abelian sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Let $e:F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G\to H$ and $e':F'\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G'\to H'$ be morphisms of sheaves, with tensor product as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Suppose given coefficient maps $a:f^{-1}F\to F'$, $b:f^{-1}G\to G'$ and $c:f^{-1}H\to H'$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] such that
$$c\circ f^{-1}e=e'\circ(a\otimes b)$$
under the canonical identification $f^{-1}(F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G)\cong f^{-1}F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}f^{-1}G$. Write $T_a^r=H^r(Y,a)\circ f^*$, and likewise $T_b^r,T_c^r$, with ordinary small-etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Write $x\smile_e y$ for the ordinary cup product induced by derived global sections, with values in the derived tensor product $F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^L G$ on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-kun-derived-tensor] (at $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$), followed by the canonical morphism $F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^L G\to F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G$ and $e$, and define $\smile_{e'}$ similarly. For all $p,q\geq0$, $x\in H^p(X,F)$ and $y\in H^q(X,G)$ one has
$$T_c^{p+q}(x\smile_e y)=T_a^p(x)\smile_{e'}T_b^q(y).$$

source.place: Tag 0H9A, label lemma-base-change-cup-product; Tag 0FPJ, label sites-cohomology-section-cup-product

proof.text: Use the one-object point site with ring $\mathbf Z$, so its module category is $\mathrm{Ab}$. For $T=X,Y$, take the global-sections geometric morphism $p_T:T_{\mathrm{Et}}\to\mathrm{pt}$, with inverse image the constant-sheaf functor and structural ring map $p_T^{-1}\mathbf Z=\mathbf Z_T$. The set-valued adjunction is [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections]. Finite limits are preserved: a finite tuple of locally constant sections is locally constant on a common refinement, and equalizers impose the same equality locally. Thus this is a ringed-topos morphism in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. On abelian groups the constant functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], since constant presheaves are sectionwise exact. The adjunction restricts to abelian groups by imposing addition and zero on both sides of its natural bijection. Its right adjoint is $M\mapsto M(T)=\Gamma(T,M)$. Consequently $Rp_{T,*}$ on a bounded-below complex $K$ is represented by $\Gamma(T,I)$ for a K-injective resolution $K\to I$, exactly the $R\Gamma(T,K)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. The identifications on morphisms also agree: both apply $\Gamma(T,-)$ to comparison maps of these same resolutions. Work in a universe making the two etale sites small. No connectedness is assumed and the point coefficient ring is $\mathbf Z$, not $\Gamma(T,\mathbf Z_T)$.

source.place: Tag 0FPJ, section-cup-product; Tag 0B6C, remark-cup-product; the structural ring is chosen to be Z

proof.text:
Put $A=Lp_X^*=p_X^{-1}$, $R=Rp_{X,*}$, $B=Lf^*=f^{-1}$, $S=Rf_*$, $C=Lp_Y^*=p_Y^{-1}$ and $T=Rp_{Y,*}$. For $B$ the exactness and constant-ring identifications are [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; for $A,C$ use Step 1. Exact functors equal their termwise derived functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. The generic ringed-topos lemma [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] gives the adjunctions $A\dashv R$, $B\dashv S$, $C\dashv T$ and K-injective direct images. [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], including its specialization to the point site, supplies the derived tensors on the three module derived categories and the natural comparisons $t_A,t_B,t_C$. Use unbounded derived categories throughout; on bounded-below objects $R,T$ are those of Step 1. By [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], the structural identification $p_Y\cong p_Xf$ gives monoidal $C\cong BA$ and adjunction-compatible $\kappa:T\xrightarrow{\sim}RS$. The structural 2-isomorphism is fixed by the equality of underived section functors $\Gamma_X f_*=\Gamma_Y$ and their adjunction bijections. In particular, under these comparisons,
$$t_C=t_B\circ B(t_A),\qquad \varepsilon^Y_E=\varepsilon^f_E\circ B(\varepsilon^X_{SE}).$$
Here $\varepsilon^X,\varepsilon^f,\varepsilon^Y$ denote the three counits. These formulas use the composite-adjunction counit, not just an isomorphism of underlying functors.

Define $\beta_K=\kappa_{BK}^{-1}\circ R(\eta^f_K):RK\to TBK$, where $\eta^f:1\to SB$ is the derived unit. This is natural in every derived morphism $K\to L$, since $\eta^f$ and $\kappa$ are natural. On bounded-below objects $\eta^f$ is the unit $\eta^D_f$ used in [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit]: the canonical adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] is induced by the underived adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ with $B=f^{-1}$ exact and $S$ computed by K-injective resolutions, so on a bounded-below complex $M$ with K-injective resolution $f^{-1}M\to J$ its unit is the class of $M\to f_*f^{-1}M\to f_*J$, which is the characterization of $\eta^D_f$ in that node's cited adjunction. For bounded-below arguments $\beta$ is therefore the pullback of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit]. To check the comparison, let $E\to J$ be a bounded-below K-injective resolution on $Y$. Clause 1 of that node says that $f_*J$ is K-injective. In the normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], choose the further resolution $f_*J\to f_*J$ to be the identity. Then $\kappa_E$ is represented by the identity on $\Gamma(Y,J)=\Gamma(X,f_*J)$. The Leray arrow $\lambda_E:RSE\to TE$ in the derived-unit node is represented by the same identity in the opposite direction. Hence $\lambda=\kappa^{-1}$, including the canonical resolution identifications, and clause 2 gives precisely $\beta$. This checks the direction of the comparison rather than assuming that two unnamed Leray isomorphisms agree.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, K-injective normalization; Tag 01F9, equation-functorial-derived

proof.text:
Define $\mu_X:RK\otimes^L RL\to R(K\otimes^L L)$ to be the adjoint of
$$m_X=(\varepsilon^X_K\otimes^L\varepsilon^X_L)\circ t_{A;RK,RL}:A(RK\otimes^L RL)\to K\otimes^L L,$$
and define $\mu_Y$ with $C,T,\varepsilon^Y$. This is the relative cup construction of Remark 0B6C, using the adjunction and tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. In particular the defining adjunction equation is
$$\varepsilon^X_{K\otimes^L L}\circ A(\mu_X)=m_X.$$
Both maps are natural in both arguments. Explicitly for $u:U\to U'$, $v:V\to V'$ on $Y$, the mates of $T(u\otimes^Lv)\mu_Y$ and $\mu_Y(Tu\otimes^LTv)$ are both $(u\varepsilon^Y_U\otimes^Lv\varepsilon^Y_V)t_C$, by naturality of $t_C$ and of $\varepsilon^Y$. Thus
$$T(u\otimes^Lv)\circ\mu_Y=\mu_Y\circ(Tu\otimes^LTv).$$
This proves the coefficient naturality of the relative cup that will be needed below.

source.place: Tag 0B6C, remark-cup-product; naturality follows by the displayed adjunction calculation

proof.text:
Compute the transpose of $\beta_K$, retaining the normalized comparisons of Steps 2–3. In the following equation $C=BA$, $T=RS$ are identified by those comparisons. The composite-adjunction counit of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon^Y_{BK}\circ C(\beta_K)
&=\varepsilon^f_{BK}\circ B(\varepsilon^X_{SBK})\circ BA R(\eta^f_K)\\
&=\varepsilon^f_{BK}\circ B(\eta^f_K)\circ B(\varepsilon^X_K)\\
&=B(\varepsilon^X_K).
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is naturality of $\varepsilon^X$ for the morphism $\eta^f_K:K\to SBK$. The last is the triangle identity $\varepsilon^f_{BK}\circ B(\eta^f_K)=1_{BK}$ of the adjunction furnished by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. This establishes the transpose formula from the actual unit and counits; it is not a clause attributed to the additive pullback lemma.

source.place: Tag 0H9A, lemma-base-change-cup-product (proof omitted); explicit unit/counit calculation supplied here

proof.text:
We now prove the required derived square:
$$T(t_{B;K,L})\circ\beta_{K\otimes^L L}\circ\mu_X
=\mu_Y\circ(\beta_K\otimes^L\beta_L).$$
Take adjoints under $C\dashv T$. By Step 5, naturality of $\varepsilon^Y$ and the defining equation of Step 4, the left-hand adjoint is
$$t_B\circ B(\varepsilon^X_{K\otimes^L L})\circ BA(\mu_X)
=t_B\circ B\bigl((\varepsilon^X_K\otimes^L\varepsilon^X_L)t_A\bigr)
=(B\varepsilon^X_K\otimes^LB\varepsilon^X_L)t_C.$$
The last equality uses naturality of $t_B$ and the monoidality of $C\cong BA$ in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. The right-hand adjoint, by naturality of $t_C$, is
$$(\varepsilon^Y_{BK}\circ C\beta_K\ \otimes^L\ \varepsilon^Y_{BL}\circ C\beta_L)t_C
=(B\varepsilon^X_K\otimes^LB\varepsilon^X_L)t_C,$$
again by Step 5. The adjunction bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] is injective, so the two derived morphisms agree. This fills the omitted square of 0H9A for the square with vertical maps $p_X,p_Y$ and bottom map $\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{pt}}$.

source.place: Tag 0H9A, lemma-base-change-cup-product, specialized to the structural square; proof supplied by the two displayed transposes

proof.text:
We also need to check the derived-to-underived tensor arrows, not just the square of Step 6. For abelian sheaves $M,N$ on either etale site, choose functorial flat resolutions $P(M)\to M[0]$, $P(N)\to N[0]$, zero in positive degrees, by [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement]. They are K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. The canonical augmentation $\delta_{M,N}:M\otimes^LN\to(M\otimes N)[0]$ is represented by the tensor of these two augmentations. The total-tensor and derived-tensor identifications, with their naturality in resolutions, are [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Thus $\delta$ is natural in sheaf morphisms: on these functorial resolutions, both composites in its naturality square are literally the tensor of the two augmented maps. For $B=f^{-1}$, exactness [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] preserves the augmentations and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] makes $BP(M),BP(N)$ valid K-flat models. On these models $t_B$ is the termwise tensor identification of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. Hence
$$\delta_{BM,BN}\circ t_{B;M,N}=q_{B;M,N}\circ B(\delta_{M,N}),$$
where $q_B:B(M\otimes N)\xrightarrow{\sim}BM\otimes BN$ is that underived identification: the square is the tensor of $BP(M)\to BM$ and $BP(N)\to BN$ in each bidegree.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor; Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, total-complex construction

proof.text:
The degree-zero normalization in Step 7 is the one in the hypothesis. Indeed a nonpositive tensor total complex has degree-zero cokernel
$$\operatorname{coker}\bigl(P(M)^{-1}\otimes P(N)^0\oplus P(M)^0\otimes P(N)^{-1}\to P(M)^0\otimes P(N)^0\bigr)=M\otimes N.$$
Tensor is right exact in each variable: [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] makes each tensor functor a left adjoint, and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] applies to the finite cokernel diagrams. Thus $H^0(\delta)$ is the displayed canonical isomorphism. Exactness of $B$ commutes with these cokernels and cohomology by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. The termwise formula in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] therefore identifies $H^0(t_B)$, under these $H^0(\delta)$ isomorphisms, with $q_B$. In particular the coefficient hypothesis means exactly
$$c\circ B(e)=e'\circ(a\otimes b)\circ q_{B;F,G}$$
as maps from $B(F\otimes G)$ to $H'$. No comparison for scheme $\mathcal O$-modules is substituted for the constant-integer sheaf tensor.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor, degree-zero augmentation; Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product

proof.text:
Put $d=e\circ\delta_{F,G}:F\otimes^LG\to H$ and $d'=e'\circ\delta_{F',G'}$. Steps 7–8 and naturality of $\delta$ give the equality of derived coefficient arrows
$$c\circ B(d)=d'\circ(a\otimes^Lb)\circ t_{B;F,G}.$$
Combining this with Steps 3, 4 and 6 now gives, with $T_a=T(a)\beta_F$ and similarly $T_b,T_c$,
$$\begin{aligned}
T_c\circ R(d)\circ\mu_X
&=T(c\circ B(d))\circ\beta_{F\otimes^LG}\circ\mu_X\\
&=T(d')\circ T(a\otimes^Lb)\circ T(t_B)\circ\beta_{F\otimes^LG}\circ\mu_X\\
&=T(d')\circ T(a\otimes^Lb)\circ\mu_Y\circ(\beta_F\otimes^L\beta_G)\\
&=T(d')\circ\mu_Y\circ(T_a\otimes^LT_b).
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality uses naturality of $\beta$ for $d$, not a claim of cup naturality from additive pullback naturality; the last is the independently proved naturality of $\mu_Y$ in Step 4. This computation takes place in unbounded derived categories, so no boundedness of $F\otimes^LG$ is assumed. Only $F,G,H$ need the bounded-below pullback identification of Step 3.

source.place: Tag 0H9A and Tag 0FPJ; substitution of the established derived square and augmentation identities

proof.text:
Pass to the canonical cohomology pairing $H^p(U)\otimes H^q(V)\to H^{p+q}(U\otimes^LV)$ in $D(\mathrm{Ab})$. For clarity, this pairing is natural: on K-flat resolutions of the already derived complexes $U,V$ it sends cycles $z,w$ to the cycle $z\otimes w$; changing either cycle by a boundary changes the result by a boundary by the signed total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], specialized to the point. Chain maps preserve this construction, and it descends through the quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], again on the point site. These are resolutions of $R\Gamma_XF,R\Gamma_XG$, not ordinary global sections of K-flat sheaf models. Apply this natural pairing and $H^{p+q}$ to Step 9. Under [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit], $H^p(T_a)=H^p(Y,a)f^*$ and likewise for $b,c$. By the relative-cup definition in Step 4 followed by $d,d'$, the resulting horizontal operations are precisely the $\smile_e,\smile_{e'}$ of the statement. Evaluating the equality of Step 9 on $x,y$ proves
$$T_c^{p+q}(x\smile_e y)=T_a^p(x)\smile_{e'}T_b^q(y).$$

source.place: Tag 0FPJ, section-cup-product; Tag 0H9A, cohomology of the proved square

proof.text: For $f=\mathrm{id}$, use the identity-adjunction and identity-tensor clauses of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]; the formula becomes the coefficient naturality proved in Steps 4 and 7. In degree $p=q=0$, Step 8 gives exactly the ordinary tensor of global sections followed by the specified pairing. If a factor is zero or the scheme is empty, both sides vanish, since the corresponding section complexes are zero. Disconnected schemes remain included because Step 1 uses the ring $\mathbf Z$ on the point throughout.

source.place: Tag 0FPJ; identity comparison and degree-zero normalization
